title: Why rockets don't just fly up — they fall sideways!
core_points: Kids already know: drop a ball, it falls. Throw a ball, it falls AND goes sideways.
The secret of orbit: rockets throw themselves sideways so fast that they keep missing the ground
The ISS is literally falling toward Earth right now — but it's moving sideways at 28,000 km/h
Fun numbers: ISS goes around Earth every 90 minutes, you'd fit 8 Earths across the orbit radius
Why we can't just 'go up' to space — air runs out, rockets get heavy, sideways is the trick
Different rockets have different jobs: big ones for cargo, small ones for astronauts, reusable ones come back
Draw-along moment: sketch your own orbit — the faster you throw, the farther around you go
What YOU could send to space: name tags, student experiments, even seeds that grow in orbit
Homework idea: toss a tennis ball harder and harder across the playground, watch the arc grow
Big idea to remember: gravity isn't the enemy of space travel, sideways speed is the secret
